issuer: New Mexico Taxation and Revenue Department
title: New Mexico TRD Ruling 225-94-1 Severance Pay
text:
Ruling 225-94-1
Issued: January 21, 1994
Effective: January 21, 1994
Revised: December 12, 2008, correction and citation updated, as indicated by brackets
A ruling has been requested concerning the applicability of certain provisions of the Income
Tax Act to the following facts:
X was a resident of Texas until August of 1991. Until June 1991 X, was employed
by Company Y. In June, 1991 Y closed the division in which X was employed. X
was granted a severance package. X received the severance pay over a twelve month
period including the last half of 1991 and the first half of 1992. In August 1991, X
moved to and became a resident of New Mexico.
X states that the severance pay received while a resident of New Mexico is not subject to
taxation under the Income Tax Act since the severance pay was for wages earned in Texas prior to
becoming a resident of New Mexico. X references the instructions for completing the Personal
Income Tax Returns which state “Only income earned while a New Mexico resident is subject to
New Mexico income tax.”
Section 7-2-3 NMSA 1978 states:
A tax is imposed at the rates specified in the Income Tax Act upon the net income
of every resident individual and upon the net income of every nonresident individual
employed or engaged in the transaction of business in, into or from this state or
deriving any income from any property or employment within this state. (Emphasis
added)
Section 7-2-11(A)(3) NMSA 1978 states "compensation of a resident [taxpayer] shall be
allocated to this state."
Taxation and Revenue Department regulation IT 11:6 [3.3.11.11(A) NMAC] states: “All
compensation received while a resident of New Mexico shall be allocated to this state whether or
not such compensation is earned from employment in this state.”
Except for accrual basis taxpayers which X does not claim to be, income generally is
“earned” for income tax purposes in the period in which it is received, not the period in which the
activity, if any, which gave rise to the income occurred. X's severance pay is reportable as
compensation in the year in which it was received. Severance pay received after X became a
resident of New Mexico is subject to the New Mexico income tax.
The New Mexico income tax imposes a tax on the total income of a resident unless there is a
specific exemption or deduction provided in the New Mexico Income Tax Act. In this case there is
no specific deduction or exemption which would authorize X to exclude the severance pay.
